# Deep First Search: Agent Safe

> Safe x402 payments for AI agents. The owner decides payees, prices and caps (in code and in an owner-signed, timelocked budget enforced by a contract on Base); the model only chooses which URL to fetch. A prompt-injected agent cannot overspend, pay a different wallet or accept a price hike. Open source, MIT. Live on Base mainnet as an unaudited beta, and on Base Sepolia.

## Packages (npm)

- `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay`: TypeScript SDK. `createAgentPay({ registry, policy, payer, session, ensureFunded? })` returns `{ commitPlan(items, ttlMs), fetch(url, init, { plan }), kill(), audit }`. Also the owner CLI (`npx @deepfirstsearch/agent-pay owner …`), an offline demo (`npx @deepfirstsearch/agent-pay demo`), `AGENT_SAFE` deployments, contract ABIs, and `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay/testing` (`startMockServer`, an offline x402 merchant).
- `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay-mcp`: MCP server (stdio). Tools: `paid_fetch(url, method?, body?, contentType?)`, `list_merchants()`, `budget_status()`. Config file holds merchants and caps; env `AGENT_PAY_AGENT_KEY`, `AGENT_PAY_BURNER_SEED`. Since 0.2.0: `merchants[].x402Versions` (default `[2]`; `[1, 2]` for x402 v1 merchants such as Heurist Mesh) and `confirmOnChain` (default `true`: an unreadable receipt is checked on-chain through `rpcUrl` instead of resent; needed for CoinMarketCap, JustaName, Glim). Without a vault it prints each merchant's payer address on start. Registry name `com.deepfirstsearch/agent-pay-mcp`.
- `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay-ai-sdk`: `paidFetchTool({ pay, plan })` for the Vercel AI SDK.
- `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay-langchain`: `createPaidFetchTool({ pay, plan })` for LangChain.js / LangGraph.
- `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay-turnkey`: `turnkeyPayer({ client, address })`, a Turnkey-held key as the payer.
- `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay-privy`: `privyPayer({ privy, walletId, address, authorizationContext? })`, a Privy server wallet as the payer (returns a viem `LocalAccount`).
- `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay-cdp`: `await cdpPayer({ cdp, name })` or `cdpPayer({ cdp, address })`, a Coinbase CDP Server Wallet account as the payer; signs only EIP-712 typed data, refuses transactions and messages.
- `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay-agentkit`: `agentPayActionProvider({ pay, plan })` for Coinbase AgentKit (action `AgentPayActionProvider_paid_fetch`, exported as `PAID_FETCH_ACTION`; input is only a URL), and `agentKitPayer(walletProvider)` to use an AgentKit EVM wallet provider as the payer. Install with `@coinbase/agentkit viem@2.38.3 zod@3`.
- `@deepfirstsearch/order-guard`: `createOrderGuard(policy, backend)` returns `{ preview, submit, spentToday, audit }`; throws `OrderRefusedError`. Owner-set limits for agents that place real orders (approved stores, pinned delivery address, order/tip caps, daily budget, single-use previews). `/testing` exports `createMockDelivery`, `MOCK_STORES`.
- The tool packages take `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay` (and `ai`/`zod`, `@langchain/core`, `@coinbase/agentkit`, the wallet SDKs, `viem`) as peer dependencies: install them alongside.

## Key rules when integrating

- Payee (`payTo`), price pin and caps come from `MerchantRegistry` and the sealed plan, never from the model or the 402 response.
- Call `pay.commitPlan(...)` before the agent reads untrusted content; pass the plan to every `pay.fetch`.
- Amounts are atomic USDC units (6 decimals) as bigint: 10_000n = 0.01 USDC.
- `payer` is any viem `LocalAccount`: a local key, or Turnkey, Privy, Coinbase CDP or KMS wrapped with `toAccount`.
- Offline testing: `startMockServer(routes, { network })` from `@deepfirstsearch/agent-pay/testing` (default Base Sepolia `eip155:84532`; pass `eip155:8453` for mainnet-shaped code). It verifies signatures locally and needs no funds.
- Extensions (agent-pay >= 0.9.0): none are echoed by default. Per merchant, `echoExtensions: ["builder-code"]` echoes that declaration back (Base Builder Codes, ERC-8021), and `builderCodes: ["bc_…"]` adds the owner's service codes as `info.s`. Echoing never changes payee, amount, asset or network.
- Per-merchant `maxTimeoutSeconds` (10 to 86400) overrides the default 300 s authorization window for that merchant only.
- Optional: `screen` (sanctions, fails closed), `confirmAuthorization: usdcAuthorizationCheck({ network: publicClient })` (on-chain confirmation when a receipt is unusable), `approve`, `settleRetries`.
- On-chain budgets: each top-up must be <= the intent's `maxPerTx` and `trancheCap`.
- Refusals throw `PaymentDeniedError` (policy) or `PaymentBlockedError` (kill switch, rate limit, settlement); integrations return them as data. Branch on codes, never on reason text (agent-pay >= 0.8.0): `PaymentDeniedError` has `codes`, `code` and `action` (`report`: possible redirection such as `payee_mismatch`, never retry; `ask_owner`: e.g. `price_changed`, `over_cap`; `fix_config`: e.g. `unknown_merchant`, `version_not_allowed`; `retry_later`: e.g. `plan_exhausted`, `budget_exhausted`), closed set `REFUSAL_CODES`. `PaymentBlockedError` has `code` and `action` (`BLOCK_CODES`): `settlement_pending` → `resend_same` (request the same resource again; the SDK resends the same proof and never re-signs), `settled_not_delivered` → `report` (never pay again; also when a merchant answers a resend with "already used"), `settlement_unknown` → `ask_owner` (agent-pay >= 0.8.2: an expired unconfirmed authorization is never followed by a second signature unless the chain says it was unused, via `confirmAuthorization`, or the owner calls `pay.forgetUnsettled(url)`), `rate_limited` → `retry_later`, `kill_switch` → `ask_owner`. Sellers without a standard receipt can send `X-Payment-Settled: true | queued` on a 2xx; it is accepted once and surfaced as `res.payment.merchantSettled`.
- Receipts: read from `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` (or `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`); the receipt's network must map to the network that was signed. v1 short names (`base`, `base-sepolia`) are mapped through a fixed table, also in v2 receipts (agent-pay >= 0.8.5); unknown names are rejected. With `X-Payment-Settled`, a well-formed `X-Payment-Tx` is reported as `settlement.transaction`.
- Replays: one signed authorization per resource. Any replay refusal from the merchant (`tx_already_used`, `nonce_already_used_locally`, `nonce_replayed_local`, "nonce already used") is classified `settled_not_delivered` and is never re-signed (agent-pay >= 0.8.4).
- 402 tolerance (agent-pay >= 0.8.3): informational option fields (`chainId`/`networkV1`, which must agree with `network`; `outputSchema`; resource metadata) are accepted and never used to sign; vendor keys at the top level of a 402 are dropped; payment terms (`payTo`, `amount`, `asset`, `network`, `to`, `recipient`, …) outside `accepts` reject the 402, as does a `payTo` that differs from the registry (merchants that rotate `payTo` per request cannot be paid).
- x402 v2 by default. x402 v1 only for merchants whose registry entry sets `x402Versions: [1, 2]` (or `[1]`); there is no global switch and no automatic downgrade; a v1 402 from any other merchant is refused (`version_not_allowed`).
- `paid_fetch` (MCP, AI SDK, LangChain, AgentKit) fetches any URL; only payments are restricted to registered merchants. Non-402 responses from other origins come back as fenced, untrusted data.
